# SCIMpy

This repo contains two things. The first is the actual SCIM implementation library (contained in the `/lib` directory) and the second one is a **Simple Implementation Server** (contained in the `scr` directory).

## The big picture.

A SCIM server is obviously a HTTP server but every API is going to be built differently. That is why the `/lib` doesn't contain any classes that have to do with the Controllers, Router and Dependency Management part. That is left up to the implementer. The Simple Implementation Server will then use the `/lib` to implement a bare-bone SCIM Server.

The `/lib` is mostly comprised of **Services**, **Models** and **Repositories**. The diagram below explained what is implemented where. The Controllers (and Routes) are in the `/src` directory. This is because the Controller/Router could be a Symphony or Laravel or Drupal or Wordpress or whatever, and doesn't have anything to do with the actual SCIM implementation.

Next come the **Services**. They are implemented in the `/lib` directory because they contain SCIM domain logic. **Services** are dependant on [PSR-7](https://www.php-fig.org/psr/psr-7/) **Request** and **Response** object. They are optionally dependent on a [PSR-14: Event Dispatcher](https://www.php-fig.org/psr/psr-14/) library.

The **Models** (or the DataTransferObjects) are implemented in `/lib`. They are part of the SCIM spec.

Then there are the **Repositories**. They are dependent on the underlying data-source (database, external system..., where the Users and Groups are stored) and how the data-source is modeled. The `/lib` directory defined some `interfaces` that need to implemented. There is a very simple example of this in the `/src` directory. That implementation uses [SQLite](https://www.sqlite.org/) and [PDO](https://www.php.net/manual/en/book.pdo.php) to persist data (Users and Groups).

In the diagram below, the **Repository** interfaces are noted with a dashed box, indicating that these are only interfaces. The implementations of these interfaces are in the `/src` directory, that is why they get a solid box. Lastly, a database is drawn on the `/src` lane, this is to indicate that the storage mechanism (database, flat-file, API calls...) is part of the implementation, not this library.

## Services
The main SCIM logic lives in the **Services**. They expect a [PSR-7](https://www.php-fig.org/psr/psr-7/) **Request** object and a [PSR-7](https://www.php-fig.org/psr/psr-7/) **Response** object. They will then return a [PSR-7](https://www.php-fig.org/psr/psr-7/) **Response** object that can be sent back to the requester/client. 

### Events
If a [PSR-14: Event Dispatcher](https://www.php-fig.org/psr/psr-14/) implementation is provided to the Services, they will dispatch events for Create, Read, Update and Delete which can be used for further processing and/or logging. Have a look at `/src/service.php` for examples.

## Repositories
This is where the data (User, Groups) are sourced/queried. This is different for every application, that is why this library only provides interfaces (which the Services depend on) and leaves the implementation up to you.
